statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-9669: a bz2.BZ2Decompressor could be reused after a decompression error, and crafted input could then make it resume from an invalid internal state and write out of bounds on a stack buffer. Upstream fixed it in https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/150599 (3.12 commit https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/991e6cf86496718c4ef00b362d640e00cb5c85b2), first released in CPython 3.12.14: a decompressor that has failed raises ValueError('Decompressor is unusable after a previous error'). See https://mail.python.org/archives/list/security-announce@python.org/thread/DBJZETMGUIFK7DVUWMOXHD3Z6IX2QPSX/ and https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-9669. Checked the _bz2 extension module for the error message the fix adds (with its existing 'End of stream already reached' message as a control) in the python-3.12 package of every build published in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository, 3.12.12-r0 to 3.12.16-r4, x86_64 and aarch64; both architectures agree. Builds before 3.12.13-r10 lack the fix; 3.12.13-r10 and every later build have it (from that build to the last CPython 3.12.13 build it is a backport made before the 3.12.14 release; the 3.12.14 and later builds carry the upstream fix). The range ends at 3.12.13-r10.
